sections.h2: What sets Newton County apart east of Atlanta?
sections.html:
Newton County is a Piedmont county in east central Georgia, anchored by Covington as the seat and largest city, and it sits inside the Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell metro area. The General Assembly created it on December 24, 1821, naming it for a sergeant who served under Gen. Francis Marion in the Revolutionary War, per Wikipedia.

Cities include Covington, Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn and the unincorporated community of Starrsville. Interstate 20 crosses the county alongside US 278, and a string of state routes branch off it. Walton, Morgan, Jasper, Butts, Henry and Rockdale counties are the neighbors. Most of the land drains to the Upper Ocmulgee River, with a slice in the east draining to the Upper Oconee.

Covington's square became a film location: the first five episodes of The Dukes of Hazzard were shot there in late 1978, and In the Heat of the Night was filmed in the city from 1988 to 1995. Most of the county is served by the Newton County School System, while parts of Social Circle belong to the Social Circle City School District.

sections.h2: How fast has Newton County grown, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Newton County grew from 41,808 residents in 1990 to 112,483 in the 2020 census, and the July 2025 estimate is 125,583. Along the way the count was 62,001 in 2000 and 99,958 in 2010, as the metro area spread east.

Workers face a mean commute of 35.9 minutes, and the county covers 273.80 square miles of land. Builders pulled 605 permits in 2025. Households average 2.83 people.

sections.h2: Which Newton County tax offices should a seller contact?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner collects, the Tax Assessors value the property and process exemptions, and the Board of Commissioners and Board of Education set the millage. The Tax Commissioner's office is elected and independent of both the assessors and the county commission, per its FAQ.

  • Admin Building: 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, Covington, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30, phone 770-784-2020
  • Westside office: 3612 Salem Rd, Covington, same hours and phone
  • Tax Assessors: 770-784-2030 for exemptions, returns and appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court deed room, Newton County Courthouse: copies of recorded deeds

The locations page also lists self-service kiosks inside two Covington Kroger stores, on Highway 20 South and Highway 278 NE. A written request for a balance can be mailed to the Admin Building address.

sections.h2: When is the Newton County property tax due?
sections.html:
Newton County property tax is due November 15 each year, a change from the old December 20 date that took effect with the 2026 tax year. The commissioners approved the move in 2025, according to the tax office's FAQ.

November 15, 2026 fell on a Sunday, so the office honored payments through Monday, November 16 without interest. Statements for real estate and personal property are mailed by September 15, and non-homesteaded mobile homes are billed by February 1 and due April 1.

  • Interest runs monthly at the prime rate plus 3% a year; the page listed .0875% per month
  • After 120 days, a 5% penalty is added to the original tax, and another 5% every 120 days until it reaches 20%
  • Only U.S. Postal Service postmarks count as proof of timely mailing; meter-dated postmarks are not honored
  • Partial payments are accepted, but interest and penalties keep accruing on the balance

Card fees, shown on the same page, are 2.35% for Visa, MasterCard and Discover and 3% for American Express, each with a $1.50 minimum; eCheck online costs a flat $1.50.

sections.h2: What is the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant in Newton County?
sections.html:
The Homeowner Tax Relief Grant is a state credit that appears as its own line on a 2026 Newton County tax bill. Eligible homesteaded properties receive an $18,000 reduction in assessed value for the benefit, and the dollar credit varies with the millage in each tax district.

No separate application is made to the Tax Commissioner; the credit goes to properties that already hold a qualifying homestead exemption. It is separate from the homestead exemption, so one bill can carry both. The office describes it as a one-time credit for the 2026 tax year only.

Sellers whose mortgage servicer pays the taxes from escrow should note that the office does not set escrow payments. A lower bill may or may not change the monthly payment, and the servicer decides.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemptions and appeals work in Newton County?
sections.html:
The homestead filing deadline is April 1, and an application is also accepted during the 45-day appeal period after assessment notices go out. You apply once and the exemption stays until ownership or your primary residence changes; exemptions do not transfer to a buyer.

  • Standard: reduces taxable value by $4,000 on county and school levies, one homestead per owner
  • Age 62: $20,000 reduction on county and school levies, net earned income cap of $15,000
  • Age 65: $30,000 off county levies and $50,000 off Newton Schools, net earned income cap of $25,000
  • Disabled veterans: reduces the 40% taxable value up to $126,526, with a Veterans Administration letter

The 62 and 65 exemptions also cap household social security and retirement income at $99,648, as printed on the homestead page. An appeal goes first to the Board of Assessors in writing within 45 days of the assessment notice, stating whether you choose the Board of Equalization path or another method.

sections.h2: What happens to Newton County liens and unpaid taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax can become a lien called a FiFa, recorded on the General Execution Docket with the Clerk of Superior Court. Before one is issued, the office mails a 30-day notice of intent to the owner of record.

A FiFa stays in effect for seven years and can be renewed without limit. It is a public record, so credit bureaus may pick it up, and paying the tax, fees, penalty and interest cancels it. The Tax Commissioner's office says it does not sell tax liens over the counter and publishes tax sale lists when a sale is scheduled.

Ask the Tax Commissioner for a written balance dated close to your closing, and have the closing agent pay it from the proceeds. Bills are mailed to the owner, never to the mortgage company, so forward yours if a servicer needs it.

faqs.q: What is the Newton County property tax due date?
faqs.a: November 15 each year, starting with the 2026 tax year. The earlier date was December 20. For 2026 the office extended the no-interest window to Monday, November 16 because November 15 landed on a Sunday.

faqs.q: How long does a Newton County owner have to appeal a value?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File the written appeal with the Board of Assessors and say which route you choose. The appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

faqs.q: Do Newton County exemptions transfer to the buyer of my house?
faqs.a: No. The tax office states that exemptions do not transfer. A new owner or a homeowner who changes primary residence must apply again, by April 1 or during the 45-day appeal period.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Newton County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Admin Building, 1113 Usher St NE, Suite 101, Covington, or the Westside office at 3612 Salem Rd. Both are open Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 4:30. Call 770-784-2020 with questions.

faqs.q: Which cities are inside Newton County?
faqs.a: Covington is the county seat. The others are Mansfield, Oxford, Porterdale and Social Circle, plus the town of Newborn. Property inside a city may carry that city's tax as well, so check the bill you receive.
